extracted.intended_audience: government policy-makers, regulators, and civil servants responsible for regulatory policy and consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, conducting, and evaluating stakeholder engagement and consultation across the regulatory policy cycle in government. Emphasises who to engage, why, how (tools and modalities), timing, follow-up, and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives of stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Why engage? Collecting better evidence, improving compliance, and strengthening legitimacy of decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should: (1) collect more diverse and well-informed inputs to address real needs of citizens; (2) increase a sense of ownership among stakeholders to improve compliance and reduce enforcement costs; (3) ensure accountability, strengthen legitimacy and help regain public trust in policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who to engage with (definition and inclusiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders are those interested and affected by regulation, potentially including citizens, businesses, trade unions, civil society organisations, public sector organisations, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation should be open and voluntary; be specific when selecting who to consult; revisit stakeholder analysis throughout the consultation process; avoid over-reliance on advisory bodies or expert groups. Keep in mind stakeholders usually least represented (e.g. new entrants, SMEs) and potentially affected foreign stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, cross-cutting policy on stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a government-wide policy with clearly set objectives for stakeholder engagement and guidance for civil servants and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should provide guidance on tools, information dissemination, and providing feedback. A central, cross-cutting policy anchors consistent expectations and practices across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms and oversight for engagement activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Define mechanisms and oversight including clear competences for coordination and promotion of stakeholder engagement across institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set responsibilities for coordination, promotion and monitoring of engagement activities to ensure consistent implementation and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning engagement actions strategically and in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan stakeholder engagement beforehand and strategically to identify when stakeholders will be engaged and select appropriate tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance planning helps choose the right modalities, timing, and target groups and supports meaningful two-way interactions rather than ad-hoc or late-stage consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and form of engagement (continuum of participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an engagement spectrum from one-way information/notification through consultation to partnership and active participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-way (information/notification) provides information; consultation enables two-way flow for obtaining information and public views and identifying conflict lines; partnership and active participation involve deeper collaboration and verification of consistency and acceptance. Select the appropriate level depending on objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modalities and types of consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a mix of consultation types such as advisory groups, broad circulation for comment, formal consultation with selected groups (e.g. social partners), informal consultation with selected groups, physical public meetings, posting on the internet without invitation to comment, public consultation on the internet with invitation to comment, virtual public meetings, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a combination of channels (physical and virtual) and tailor the modality to stage of rulemaking and stakeholder needs. OECD data highlights widespread use of advisory groups, internet consultations (with/without invitation), and meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ICT and digital tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit full potential of information and communication technologies (ICT) to enhance stakeholder engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OECD notes the full potential of ICT remains to be exploited; digital tools can broaden reach, facilitate submissions, host virtual meetings, and enable online consultations but should be used strategically and inclusively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up and feedback obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide feedback to participants and follow up on inputs received; include consideration of consultation comments in decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligations may include formally considering comments when developing the final regulation, publishing a response to consultation comments online, responding in writing to authors of comments, including views expressed in the Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA), and making participants' views public. OECD data tracks whether regulators are required to consider comments, publish responses, and respond to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: engage throughout the regulatory policy cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage stakeholders at each stage of the life-cycle of regulation rather than only late in the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should occur throughout the regulatory policy cycle to inform problem identification, design, implementation and ex post evaluation. OECD finds a trend that consultation tends to happen at a late stage — practitioners should aim to engage earlier for greater impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular evaluation of engagement policy and practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Regularly evaluate stakeholder engagement policy and practices to ensure effectiveness and meaningful participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evaluation mechanisms as part of the policy framework and use findings to improve design, timing, modalities and inclusiveness of future engagement activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage all interested and affected parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure engagement reaches all interested and affected parties, including under-represented groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design outreach and tools to reduce barriers for groups like SMEs and new market entrants, and consider potentially affected foreign stakeholders. Being specific in selection and proactive outreach helps avoid skewed representation.
